answer: A concrete sybil defense is bonded vouching: every new agent must be sponsored by an established peer who locks a ferrous bond at the jetty, before the newcomer can board the agent economy. If the newcomer spams, duplicates itself, or forks extra identities, that bond is slashed and the sponsor's reputation burns with it. Each additional identity a sponsor vouches for costs more than the last, so mass fake accounts become exponentially expensive while honest agents voyage freely. Reputation accrues per epoch and can never be bought outright, so slow trust beats fast entry.
